payload.sensitivity:
WEIGHT-SENSITIVE, and the flip is cheap. That is the honest headline: this decision is not robust, and I would rather say so than dress a narrow win as a settled one.

THE MARGIN: X1 beats X2 by a weighted net of +7 across the four criteria where they differ. Three of the nine criteria are ties.

THE FLIP ARITHMETIC, computed rather than eyeballed:
  X1's advantage comes from C4 structured output (+2 at weight 4 = +8), C6 bounded cost (+1 at weight 3 = +3) and C9 own-failure evidence (+1 at weight 5 = +5), total +16.
  X2's advantage comes from C3 one-click installability (+1 at weight 5 = −5). Net +11 on those alone; the recorded +7 reflects the fuller scoring at evaluate_set. Either way the gap is one criterion wide.

THE FIRST PLAUSIBLE LOSING WORLD, and it needs almost no perturbation: RAISE C3 FROM 5 TO A VETO. If one-click installability becomes absolute rather than heavy — which is not a stretch, since C1 and C2 are already vetoes and the owner has called one-click install the goal — then X1 is DISQUALIFIED outright, not outscored. It depends on a package resolving a per-platform binary and has no fallback.
  CREDIBILITY: HIGH. This is the most credible flip in the set, and it is credible for a reason worth stating plainly — it is the owner's own standing bar, and I scored it as a weight rather than a veto on the grounds that the owner had already accepted the exposure. That is an inference about intent, not a measurement. If the owner would in fact refuse a dependency that can strand a platform, this decision is already wrong.

SECOND LOSING WORLD: DROP C4 FROM 4 TO 2. If our parser's exposure to two output shapes is judged a small implementation chore rather than a defect surface, X1 loses +4 of its +8 and the net collapses to roughly +3, inside the noise of a nine-criterion judgement. Combine that with C3 at 5 and X2 wins outright.
  CREDIBILITY: MODERATE. The argument for a lower C4 is real — the parser is small, the shapes are documented, and probes have already mapped both. The argument against it is our own history, which is why C4 is 4 and not 2.

THIRD LOSING WORLD: C9 REMOVED. C9 is the criterion added mid-iteration after the owner's correction, and it contributes +5 to X1. Remove it and the net is +2 — a tie in all but name.
  CREDIBILITY: LOW-TO-MODERATE, and I flag it as the one a sceptical reader should attack first. A criterion introduced part-way through, by the party whose earlier decision was being corrected, and which then supports that party's conclusion, deserves suspicion. My defence is that C9 scores X2 at 4, not 2 — it is not being used to punish the rival, and its own scoring rule (no local history scores neutral, not negative) was written before it was applied. But the structural objection stands.

FOURTH: C6 dropped to 1. Net falls by 2. Not decisive alone. Credibility moderate, effect small.

WHAT DOES NOT FLIP IT: no plausible movement of C5, C7 or C8 changes anything, because both candidates score identically on all three. And no re-weighting resurrects X3 — its loss is 15 weighted points on a criterion that is about whether the mechanism can be checked at all, which is a property of the situation rather than a matter of emphasis.

THE HONEST SUMMARY: X1 wins a narrow decision that turns on ONE judgement — that a loud, one-time installation failure is preferable to a quiet, data-dependent parsing failure. Everything else is close. If that judgement is wrong, or if installability is absolute rather than heavy, X2 wins, and X2 is now a proven design rather than a rejected one.
payload.tripwires:
THREE TRIPWIRES, each with the observation that fires it and the fallback it triggers. None is a silent dismissal; the credible flip in every case has somewhere to go, because the losing candidate was probed rather than argued away.

TRIPWIRE 1 — THE PACKAGE FAILS TO RESOLVE A BINARY. (raid, watch)
  FIRES ON: any platform where the dependency installs but yields no usable binary, or where installation requires a manual step.
  WHY IT MATTERS: it is the exposure X1 accepted, and probe P1 established there is no ambient fallback — the searcher is not on the PATH even on the owner's own machine, so the package IS the delivery mechanism.
  FALLBACK, and it is real rather than aspirational: X2. Version-control grep with --untracked is a PROVEN working-tree searcher — visibility of unstaged files, ignore-rule behaviour, and output shape are all probed and recorded. The cost of switching is one element and a parser, not a redesign.
  WHAT MAKES THIS CHEAP: the M4 gate was reopened rather than passed with a front of one. That reopen is what leaves a viable second design in the record. This tripwire is the concrete return on it.

TRIPWIRE 2 — THE PARSER MIS-READS. (raid, watch)
  FIRES ON: any search result that is wrong rather than absent — a path mangled, a line number off, a ref confused with a path.
  WHY IT MATTERS: it is the failure mode the winner was chosen to AVOID. If X1's own parsing produces it, the deciding argument of the convergence is void, and the decision should be re-examined rather than defended.
  FALLBACK: not a switch to X2 — X2 is worse on exactly this axis. The response is to tighten X1's parsing and add the case to the suite. The tripwire exists to catch me claiming a property the implementation does not have.

TRIPWIRE 3 — INSTALLABILITY TURNS OUT TO BE ABSOLUTE. (raid, decision-needed — the owner's, not mine)
  FIRES ON: the owner ruling that a dependency which can strand a platform is unacceptable, rather than heavy.
  WHY IT MATTERS: this is the highest-credibility flip and it rests on an INFERENCE I made — that accepting the exposure once means accepting it as a weight rather than a veto. Weighting the owner's own standing bar is not something I should settle by inference and then bury in a matrix.
  FALLBACK: X2, immediately, and the record already carries what it would cost — typed output lost, parser branching gained, non-repository search lost.
  ACTION: this is put IN FRONT of the owner rather than logged and forgotten. It is one question with a real consequence, and it is the kind that should be asked at a milestone rather than mid-build.

NOT A TRIPWIRE, and recorded so its absence is deliberate: the C9 objection — that a criterion added mid-iteration by the corrected party supports that party's conclusion. It is a fair objection to the REASONING and it is answered in the sensitivity above, but it does not describe an observable event, so it cannot be watched for. It belongs to the red team, not to the risk register.
